Headline: Finns lost over €70m to scammers last year
Full_Text: These types of crimes increased significantly compared to 2024. Using various schemes, criminals swiped a total of around 70 million euros from victims in Finland in 2025, according to Finance Finland (FFI). FFI represents the financial interests of the country's financial sector. According to FFI, phishing scams were the most common method criminals used in bilking people out of their money, stealing around 22 million that way. In total, there were attempts to defraud people in the country of around 150 million euros last year. However, banks managed to claw back or block payments that were headed to the criminals, FFI noted. These types of crimes have increased significantly compared to 2024, when there were attempts to defraud people in Finland of around 107 million euros. That year, banks were able to retrieve or block around 40 percent of the payments.
